_meta.describes: Overall rating reported by the native best-overall routine with exactly one attribute raised and the other 20 left at the 25 floor.
_meta.warning: SEMANTICS UNVERIFIED - DO NOT TREAT AS A COST CURVE. This file could NOT be reproduced from tuning/progression_attributes.txt, unlike every other file in overall/. Only the 21 all-floor rows match a reimplementation. 14 of the 21 attributes report exactly 25.0 at every rating, and the 7 that move only do so in the top few points of their range (three_point first moves at 88, close_shot at 94). The values look saturated against the 25 floor, meaning the routine was probably called in a configuration that was never pinned down. Retained as a raw measurement for anyone who resolves the routine; not safe to build on.
_meta.source: native probe, first capture run; this measurement was not repeated
_meta.coverage: Sparse by construction: each attribute was swept from 25 up to its ceiling at the reference body, not to 99. That is why there are 1,328 rows rather than 21 x 75 = 1,575, and it exactly matches bodies/attribute_caps_sample.json.
_meta.if_you_want_a_cost_curve: Derive it from tuning/progression_attributes.txt. That math is confirmed against overall/mixed_vectors.json on all 256 vectors.
